{{Protagonists}}
{{Quote|Man, what the hood done for me? Always dragging me down. Ever since I got out of the hood shit been cracking! That's everybody's dream, to get out of the hood...|Carl Johnson to [[Sweet Johnson|Sweet]] in [[Home Coming]].|sound=CarlJohnson-GTASA-Quote.ogg}}
'''Carl''' "'''CJ'''" '''Johnson''' is the [[protagonist]] of {{SA}}.

CJ is voiced by Chris Bellard, known from the stage name [[Young Maylay]], who is also the younger cousin of [[Shawn Fonteno]], who voiced [[Franklin Clinton]] in [[Grand Theft Auto V]].

==History==
===Overview===
Carl is the second-in-command of the [[Grove Street Families]], a [[Los Santos (3D Universe)|Los Santos]]-based street gang led by his older brother, [[Sweet Johnson|Sean "Sweet" Johnson]], which also includes his childhood friends [[Ryder|Lance "Ryder" Wilson]] and [[Big Smoke|Melvin "Big Smoke" Harris]]. Having left his friends and family behind and moved to [[Liberty City (3D Universe)|Liberty City]] for five years after the death of his younger brother [[Brian Johnson|Brian]], Carl eventually returns home after learning about the murder of his mother, [[Beverly Johnson]]. From there, he works to earn back the trust of his friends and family, restore the Families to power, and learn the mysterious circumstances of his mother's death.

After being betrayed by his friends and learning of their involvement in the attack that killed his mother, Carl is exiled from Los Santos by the corrupt [[Community Resources Against Street Hoodlums|C.R.A.S.H.]] police unit. Abandoning his gang life once again, he makes new allies and becomes a successful and wealthy businessman, with assets in both [[San Fierro (3D Universe)|San Fierro]] and [[Las Venturas (3D Universe)|Las Venturas]]. He eventually returns to Los Santos to reunite with his family and is persuaded by Sweet to rebuild the Families' strength and exact revenge on those who wronged them.

Carl is the son of Beverly Johnson, the younger brother of Sweet, and the older brother of [[Kendl Johnson|Kendl]] and Brian Johnson.

===Background===
====Childhood====
Carl "CJ" Johnson was born in Los Santos to Beverly Johnson and an unnamed father; in [[The Introduction]], he mentions that he did not know his father. Beverly had four children: Sean, Carl, Kendl, and Brian. Sweet states that Carl was born in the [[Johnson House]], the family's childhood and current home. [[Old Reece]], a family friend and local barber, recalls memories of Carl's father, although Carl tells [[Joey Leone]] that he never knew his father, and that Sweet was the "man" of the house, but made his life miserable. Carl mentions to [[Wu Zi Mu|Woozie]] in [[Amphibious Assault]] that, when he was swimming as a child, he once got a condom stuck to his face, and that ''"horror like that stays with you for life"''. This also explains his fear of [[swimming]].

The Johnson siblings, along with Big Smoke and Ryder, grew up on the same [[Grove Street (3D Universe)|cul-de-sac]] and were childhood friends. CJ recalls Ryder dealing [[drugs]] since he was ten. Sweet became the leader of the Grove Street Families and introduced him, CJ, and possibly Brian into the gang life.

Around [[1985]], the Grove Street Families were at the height of their power when they first became pressured by [[Frank Tenpenny]], a corrupt police officer of C.R.A.S.H. The Families subsequently went into a decline at some point between [[1987]] and [[1992]].

Carl's younger brother Brian died in 1987. The cause of his death was never revealed, though it is implied that Carl was present, but did not help him, as Sweet laments that Carl "let Brian die". Carl was no longer considered a member of Grove Street and would later have to earn his way back into the gang. Big Smoke also [[Sweet & Kendl|implies]] that Carl was physically larger during that time, stating that the "[[Liberty City (3D Universe)|East Coast]] got [him] all thinned out".

====Adult Life in Liberty City====
Following Brian's death, Carl left Los Santos and moved to Liberty City. Sometime after his arrival, he began working for Joey Leone, the son of [[Leone Crime Family]] [[Gang Leaders|Don]] [[Salvatore Leone]], stealing cars for his [[Joey's Auto Painting|garage]]. He also committed various other small-time crimes for money.

===Events of ''Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas''===
{{Main|Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas}}
In 1992, Beverly Johnson is killed in a [[Drive-By Shooting|drive-by shooting]] by members of the [[Ballas (3D Universe)|Ballas]]. Sweet phones Carl and informs him, and Carl agrees to return to Los Santos for the funeral.

Carl flies back home and takes a taxi to his mother's house, but is soon [[In the Beginning|arrested and confronted]] by C.R.A.S.H. members [[Frank Tenpenny]], [[Eddie Pulaski]], and [[Jimmy Hernandez]], who explain that Carl will work for them whenever they call upon him; otherwise, they will frame him for killing their fellow officer [[Ralph Pendelbury]] (who was really murdered by C.R.A.S.H. themselves). After [[Big Smoke (mission)|meeting]] with Big Smoke at the Johnson house, Carl finally reunites with his siblings and friends.

Carl quickly learns that the Grove Street Families lost much of their power over the last five years {{nd}} a result of the growing crack [[cocaine]] trend and, though Sweet doesn't admit it, Sweet not having as much personal strength as a leader without CJ home. Carl and Sweet work furiously to bring the gang back to power, with Carl regaining his brother's respect in the process. This includes [[Reuniting the Families|reuniting]] with the [[Seville Boulevard Families|Seville Boulevard]] and [[Temple Drive Families]], and [[Cesar Vialpando (mission)|developing a friendship]] with [[Varrios Los Aztecas (3D Universe)|Aztecas]] leader [[Cesar Vialpando]] (who is dating Kendl, much to Sweet's disapproval). Carl also considerably weakens the Ballas, the sworn enemies of the Grove Street Families, and assists his friend [[OG Loc (3D Universe)|OG Loc]], a laughable "poser" who aspires to become a successful rapper (ruining the career of [[Madd Dogg (3D Universe)|Madd Dogg]] in the process).

Thanks to Carl's efforts, the Grove Street Families are at the second height of their power, and Sweet plans to eliminate the remaining Ballas in a large ambush. Carl prepares to join his brother and fellow gang members until Cesar calls him and reveals that [[The Green Sabre|Ryder and Big Smoke have betrayed the gang to C.R.A.S.H and the Ballas]]. Carl rushes to the gunfight, suspecting that Sweet and the other Families members are walking into a trap. He manages to hold off the Ballas to protect a heavily wounded Sweet, until both of them are arrested by the police. The Grove Street Families and the Varrios Los Aztecas practically disappear, and Big Smoke becomes the head of a powerful drug empire, taking over Los Santos. OG Loc also becomes a rich and famous rapper, with Big Smoke acting as his manager as a means to launder his money.

While Sweet is imprisoned, C.R.A.S.H. forbids Carl from returning to Los Santos and abandons him in rural [[Whetstone]] to [[Badlands|eliminate a witness against them]]. It is slowly revealed that they are being tried in court over their corruption, in a case that is quickly building media attention. Cesar connects Carl to his (mentally unstable) cousin, [[Catalina]], and the two form a relationship built on the robberies they commit together. Tenpenny [[Body Harvest|introduces]] Carl to [[The Truth]], an aging hippie who is supplying Tenpenny with tons of [[weed]], and tells Carl to [[555 We Tip|frame]] a [[District Attorney|D.A.]] who possesses evidence against C.R.A.S.H. Tenpenny demands that Carl pay for the drugs with his own money, forcing him to return to work with Catalina, who now has an obsessive crush on him.

Carl also meets [[San Fierro Triads]] leader Wu Zi Mu during a [[Wu Zi Mu (mission)|street race]]. Catalina [[Farewell, My Love...|finds]] Carl at the race and expresses her feelings of neglect and anger, feeling that he was only interested in her as a partner in crime, while also proclaiming that she has a new boyfriend, [[Claude]]. Carl defeats Claude and Catalina in a street race, gaining the deed to Claude's run-down [[Doherty Garage|garage]] in [[San Fierro (3D Universe)|San Fierro]]. CJ then leaves for San Fierro with The Truth and Tenpenny's marijuana, being forced to [[Are You Going to San Fierro?|escape from the police]] after Tenpenny betrayed The Truth. Once in the city, Carl meets Cesar and Kendl (whom he had earlier [[King in Exile|told]] to leave Los Santos for their own safety) at his new garage in [[Doherty (3D Universe)|Doherty]]. CJ is initially furious with the derelict state of the garage, but Kendl convinces him to turn it into a business opportunity. Through The Truth, Carl [[Wear Flowers in Your Hair|meets]] and hires [[Dwaine]], [[Jethro]], and [[Zero]] to work at the garage, intending to turn it into a profitable chop shop.

Carl [[Mountain Cloud Boys (mission)|meets]] with Woozie in San Fierro and the two quickly become strong allies, collaborating to take down their mutual enemies: the [[Da Nang Boys]], a [[Vietnam]]ese gang of human traffickers, and the [[Loco Syndicate]], a drug cartel supplying Big Smoke with crack cocaine. Carl [[Jizzy (mission)|infiltrates]] the Loco Syndicate and eventually kills most of its chief members. During this time, CJ continues to run his new garage, using it as a front for a car theft ring. He also purchases the [[Wang Cars (GTA San Andreas)|Wang Cars]] showroom and Zero's [[Zero RC|RC shop]] to use as legitimate fronts, earning him even more money.

Eventually, Carl receives a surprise phone call from [[Mike Toreno]], a former member of the Loco Syndicate, who survived [[Toreno's Last Flight|Carl's attempt on his life]]. Toreno [[Highjack|reveals]] himself as a government agent and enlists Carl's help with several off-the-books operations in exchange for securing Sweet's release from prison. As part of his work for Toreno, Carl [[Verdant Meadows (mission)|purchases]] an [[Verdant Meadows Airfield|abandoned airfield]] and [[Learning to Fly|learns to fly aircraft]]. Although it is a well-kept secret from all of his friends, The Truth finds Carl at his new base of operations and warns him that Toreno can't be trusted. He also recruits Carl to [[Black Project|retrieve]] a [[Jetpack]] from [[Area 69 (3D Universe)|Area 69]], which is later used to [[Green Goo|steal]] some mysterious, enlightening [[Green Goo (artifact)|green goo]] from a [[Military (3D Universe)|military]] [[Freight|train]].

Woozie [[Fender Ketchup|invites]] CJ to the Triad's glamorous [[The Four Dragons Casino|Four Dragons Casino]] in Las Venturas. Upon arrival, Carl is given shares in the casino by Woozie "in exchange for some help setting it up". They are faced with aggressive competition from the [[Mafia]]-run [[Caligula's Palace]] and, as revenge, spend time planning an [[Breaking the Bank at Caligula's|extremely elaborate heist]] on Caligula's. This involves Carl infiltrating Caligula's inner circle of management (by chance of The Truth's association with music industry employees [[Kent Paul]] and [[Maccer]]) and working with [[Ken Rosenberg]] and even Don Salvatore Leone, before helping Ken, Kent, and Maccer [[Saint Mark's Bistro|fake their deaths]] to escape Salvatore's rage.

During this time period, C.R.A.S.H. [[Misappropriation|extracts]] the last of Carl's labor before they try to kill him (as well as Hernandez for snitching on them). Hernandez is murdered, but Carl [[High Noon|survives and kills Pulaski]]. By chance, Carl also crosses paths with Madd Dogg when he saves him from a [[Madd Dogg (mission)|suicide attempt]], partially out of guilt for ruining his career. In gratitude, Madd Dogg makes Carl an offer to become his manager, which the latter accepts.

Carl's ongoing vendetta towards Tenpenny and Big Smoke, finalized by Madd Dogg having to sell his [[Madd Dogg's Crib|mansion]] to drug lord [[Big Poppa]], prompts Carl to return to Los Santos and [[A Home in the Hills|take back the rapper's mansion by force]]. While recording Madd Dogg's new album, Toreno contacts Carl and gives him [[Vertical Bird|one last task to complete]] before Sweet is released from prison. Sweet is disgusted at Carl for his new millionaire lifestyle and for having forgotten about helping the Grove Street Families, and takes him back to [[Grove Street (3D Universe)|Grove Street]] to [[Home Coming|begin]] their task of [[Beat Down on B Dup|reclaiming]] the gang's turf. As the Families slowly begin their third [[Grove 4 Life|rise]] to power, Carl manages to [[Cut Throat Business|get Madd Dogg's rhyme book]] back from OG Loc, reviving Madd Dogg's career, as well as hitting Big Smoke close to home.

During this time, Tenpenny is arrested for his crimes (thanks to Hernandez ratting him out), but is acquitted in his trial due to a lack of evidence implicating him in criminal activities. With the trial being widely covered by the media, its outcome infuriates the residents of Los Santos, who [[Riot (GTA San Andreas)|riot]] as a result. Amidst all the chaos in the city, Carl helps the Grove Street Families become the strongest gang in Los Santos at the expense of their rivals, and even assists Cesar in [[Los Desperados|retaking the Varrios Los Aztecas' turf]]. After tracking down Big Smoke, Carl [[End of the Line|storms]] his [[Big Smoke's Crack Palace|crack palace]] and kills his former friend, before he and Sweet chase Tenpenny, who tries to flee the city. The chase ends with Tenpenny being mortally injured after his firetruck falls from the bridge above Grove Street, where Carl proceeds to taunt the dying officer alongside his allies.

Later, during a celebration inside the Johnson House, Madd Dogg, accompanied by Ken, Kent, and Maccer, arrives to announce "''our'' first gold record" to Carl. At the same time, Sweet insists on making Grove Street a priority, while Kendl suggests attending to their businesses in San Fierro and Las Venturas. Carl, unsure what path to take next, decides to head outside, telling his friends and family that he's "fittin' to hit the block, see what's happening".

===After ''Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas''===
{{Speculation}}
At the very end of the game, Carl is a young and wealthy man. His assets and business interests include the Grove Street Families gang and Madd Dogg's contract in Los Santos, a car garage and several other properties in San Fierro, and shares in The Four Dragons Casino in Las Venturas, as well as the government's $60 million jetpack.

It is suggested that Carl, Madd Dogg, Kent Paul and Maccer are to go on a worldwide tour, as mentioned by Madd Dogg during the game's final [[Cutscenes|cutscene]]. Maccer and Kent Paul are to ride along, giving another hint that Carl helped the two rebuild their [[The Gurning Chimps (3D Universe)|band]].

==Further Notes==
An [[Secrets and Easter Eggs in GTA IV#References to Previous Games|Easter egg]] in {{IV}} suggests that Carl, along with the other {{3D}} [[protagonist]]s, is dead. However, this is simply to commemorate the game being the beginning of a new era and it is not considered [[canon]]. [[Rockstar Games]] have stated this is ''"a little joke to our fans"''.

==Character==
===Personality===
CJ is markedly different from the previous playable characters in the {{S}}. While [[Claude]] and [[Tommy Vercetti]] are both depicted as extremely immoral and feeling little to no regret for all of the people that they kill, CJ is depicted as having a considerably less violent personality, occasionally giving his targets a chance to redeem themselves. An example is his failed attempt at convincing Eddie Pulaski to see that he was no more than Tenpenny's pawn in the mission [[High Noon]]. Furthermore, CJ displays genuine remorse for having to kill [[Ryder]] and [[Big Smoke]], who he considered close friends. Despite his empathy, CJ doesn't seem to feel any remorse when innocent people might get hurt by his actions. This is best seen during [[Management Issues]] where CJ also kills a [[Alan Crawford's Female Associate|woman]] accompanying [[Alan Crawford]], despite only being tasked to kill the latter. Another example is CJ wasting an unassociated valet just to get his uniform during [[555 We Tip]]. In [[Architectural Espionage]], if the player doesn't have a [[camera]] before starting the mission, CJ will forcefully steal a camera by hurting a random tourist. CJ also has no problem with killing members of other gangs, and willfully slaughters any that get in his way of reclaiming [[Grove Street Families]] turf or try to sabotage his businesses, though in return, the gangsters are also trying to kill CJ.

CJ's naïve personality, face-value interpretations of other characters' responses occasionally leads them to question CJ's intelligence (namely [[The Truth]] and [[Catalina]]). Despite his mostly calm nature, CJ has shown a very violent and aggressive side when his family is threatened, as with the mission [[Deconstruction]], in which he vows to teach a lesson to the construction workers who insulted his sister, [[Kendl Johnson|Kendl]], ultimately killing them all and burying the [[Construction Foreman|foreman]] alive in a portable toilet. CJ, like his brother [[Sweet Johnson|Sweet]], holds a deep-seated loyalty towards Grove Street and the hood, as seen in his reaction to the resentful attitude of his friends and siblings early on. Though, towards the end of the game, while Sweet is in prison, and CJ is making progress in [[San Fierro (3D Universe)|San Fierro]] and [[Las Venturas (3D Universe)|Las Venturas]], the unattended Grove Street becomes [[Ballas (3D Universe)|Ballas]] turf and is filled with [[Crack Dealers|crack dealers]]. CJ tries to get his brother to abandon the hood for their assets elsewhere, but he is quickly convinced into re-taking the turf and rebuilding the Grove Street Families. Despite his young age, Carl often handles situations in a professional manner. This is shown during the mission [[The Meat Business]] when Carl keeps encouraging [[Ken Rosenberg]] to calm down and remember that "you're the boss".

At the beginning of the game, Carl, much like Sweet, has a very gang-based and ghetto mentality, stubbornly holding to his gangster views and beliefs, such as his unwillingness to "rat" towards the cops, holding onto his "street code" and naïvely believing that other gangsters also hold onto them, and using outdated methods to create tools, such as a [[Suppressor|silencer]]. Shortly after being [[The Green Sabre|exiled from Los Santos]], Carl continues to hold onto these beliefs until [[Cesar Vialpando]] reveals that Smoke was a drug dealer for a long time and was transporting drugs from San Fierro, and Kendl notes that Smoke's [[Big Smoke's House|house]] was purchased with drug money.

However, shortly after his arrival in San Fierro, Carl gradually loses his gang-based mentality and adopts more strategic, intelligent, and cunning viewpoints and mentality. This is demonstrated by [[555 We Tip|planting drugs]] in a [[District Attorney|D.A.'s]] [[Merit|car]] and reporting to the [[San Fierro Police Department|SFPD]], [[Lure (GTA San Andreas)|leading the Da Nang Boys away from Chinatown]] to allow a [[San Fierro Triads|Triad]] [[Ran Fa Li|leader]] to escape assassination, [[Puncture Wounds|using stinger traps]] to steal a [[Stratum (3D Universe)|car]] without damaging it, [[Fender Ketchup|scaring a high-ranking mobster]] into revealing his identity, planning a [[Breaking the Bank at Caligula's|major casino heist]] in Las Venturas, [[Madd Dogg (mission)|saving Madd Dogg's life]] by using a [[Walton|truck]] full of crates, [[A Home in the Hills|leading an all-out assault]] with the Triads to reclaim [[Madd Dogg (3D Universe)|Madd Dogg]]'s [[Madd Dogg's Crib|mansion]] from the [[Los Santos Vagos (3D Universe)|Vagos]], and [[End of the Line|using a SWAT Tank]] to break into a heavily protected building. Carl also becomes the successful manager of Madd Dogg, and through his various connections, helps revitalize Madd Dogg's career, further showing Carl's growing mindset and business-like methods.

However, some of CJ's actions still seem to be less thought through, with CJ seemingly hoping the situations will end well for him. The best example is going to interact with [[Johnny Sindacco]] personally on two occasions, despite knowing he will recognize him after the ordeal in [[Fender Ketchup]].

===Appearance===
In the [[Beta Content in GTA San Andreas|beta version]] and in [[The Introduction]], CJ is seen wearing a black hoodie or combat green jacket with blue jeans or beige khaki and brown shoes or white shoes or black shoes. CJ's default appearance in the final version of the game is a white tank top, with blue jeans and black tennis shoes. He is an young African-American man with a cesar hairstyle, black hair, brown eyes, a bit of facial hair and a thin body. CJ has been compared to and confused for both his father and his brother Brian, suggesting that CJ bears a great resemblance to both of them. CJ is also stated to have been fatter or more muscular before he left for [[Liberty City (3D Universe)|Liberty City]], with his friends stating the {{WP|East Coast of the United States|East Coast}} "thinned him out". Carl is noticeably short, as the player can see when Carl is standing next to other characters such as Sweet, Big Smoke, Grove Street members, and even Ryder, who has been belittled for his height numerous times. Some mission cutscenes show Carl slightly limping his left foot. This is also notable if the player enters the slow motion [[Cheats in GTA San Andreas|cheat]] twice and watches the [[sprint]] animation carefully.

CJ can have a large variety of appearances depending on the player. For example, he can wear cheap clothes from [[Binco (3D Universe)|Binco]] or luxury clothes from [[ZIP (3D Universe)|ZIP]] including green ones to represent [[Grove Street Families]]. He can be muscular, thin or fat with the use of [[gyms]] and restaurants and cheats like LifesABeach and LoveConquerSall if muscular or fat and thin are combined with use of two cheats. He can also have different [[Tattoo Parlors/GTA San Andreas|tattoos]] and [[Barbers/Hairstyles in GTA San Andreas|hairstyles]]. Carl was the most customizable protagonist until the release of {{O}}.

Another interesting dynamic thing about Carl's appearance is that his quotes depend on his clothing and physical appearance. For example, he will use more slang when dressed in lower-end clothing, speak in a more refined tone when wearing high-end clothes, or even make food-related comments when he is fatter.

The only thing that cannot be changed are CJ's underpants and he will never be naked without his clothes and underwear.

==Trivia==
===General===
*When [[Rockstar Games]] revealed that Carl was black, there was considerable uproar in the media regarding the possibility of racism.{{fact}}
*In the {{V}} mission [[Derailed]], there is a challenge for the mission, which is "Better than CJ".
**This is a reference to [[Wrong Side of the Tracks]], where CJ and [[Big Smoke]] chase a train on a [[Sanchez]] motorbike.

===''Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas''===
*On rare occasions, [[Motor Officer|motor officers]] may call out Carl by his last name or nickname when he is arrested. Members of most street gangs also recognise him (this includes all [[Los Santos (3D Universe)|Los Santos]] based gangs, the [[San Fierro Rifa]] and the [[Da Nang Boys]]).
*Carl's [[Shamal]] call sign in [[Saint Mark's Bistro]] is CJ101.
*Some of Carl's {{WP|idle animations}} consist of him singing "{{WP|Nuthin' But a 'G' Thang|Nuthin' But A G Thang Babe}}", "{{WP|Express Yourself (N.W.A song)|Express yourself, cuz I'm from Grove Street}}", "{{WP|My Lovin' (You're Never Gonna Get It)|Never gonna get it, never gonna get it, biatch}}", "{{WP|You Dropped a Bomb on Me|you drop the bomb on me}}", "{{WP|Move Your Body (Marshall Jefferson song)|move your body, dum-dah-dum, move your body}}", "{{WP|Lyn Collins|take your time and let me LOVE you girl}}" "{{WP|Love Rollercoaster|Rollercoaster! OH-OO-HOO-HOO!}}", or just humming.
*It is possible that CJ is a {{WP|Christianity|Christian}}. In the mission [[First Date (GTA San Andreas)|First Date]], Carl tells [[Catalina]] that he is a "God fearing peace-loving man of the people". Like [[Franklin Clinton]], Carl can purchase several religious [[Tattoo Parlors/GTA San Andreas|tattoos]] (most notably a {{WP|Mary, mother of Jesus|Virgin Mary}} tattoo and a cross) and a cross chain sold at [[Didier Sachs (3D Universe)|Didier Sachs]], further supporting this theory.
**However, Carl may have told that to Catalina sarcastically, especially given the actions that CJ commits throughout the storyline. In addition, in the opening [[Cutscenes|cutscene]], Big Smoke references "the book" (presumably the {{WP|Bible}}), to which Carl replies, "what fucking book?", implying he's unfamiliar with religion.
*If CJ becomes fat enough, his head will always face slightly to the side when standing still.
